requirements.text: Acceptance supports a versioned toolchain review domain without changing Phase service behavior.
Toolchain policy covers repository workflow control-plane paths and explicitly declared shared Phase entrypoints.
Policy resolution fails closed for unsupported domains, uncovered changed paths, stale policy revisions, and substituted identities.
One compact-VDD projector builds all prerequisites from explicit plan and candidate inputs without repository-wide dirty inference.
Dirty candidate bytes are frozen under the target plan and complete baseline/candidate manifests bind additions, modifications, and deletions.
The projection emits a typed run request, action DAG, command registry, and non-authorizing contract binding consumable by Acceptance.
Historical Phase inputs and artifact-only Acceptance runs remain readable and are never auto-migrated.
Package closure, docs, and terminal replay prove the new route without granting acceptance, Bootstrap, release, or archive authority.

acceptance.assertion: A schema-valid run input accepts phase_service and toolchain only.
Existing Phase policy tests and CLI aliases remain green.
Toolchain policy activates every declared workflow control-plane changed path.
Shared Phase entrypoint coverage is explicit and evidence-visible.
Unknown domains, stale policies, and uncovered paths fail closed.
Projection requires one explicit completed compact VDD target and explicit changed paths.
Unrelated dirty paths cannot enter the candidate implicitly.
Frozen dirty snapshot bytes reproduce every present candidate hash.
Manifest deletion tombstones bind baseline bytes.
All prerequisite artifacts are hash-bound, closed, and carry authorizes empty.
Existing phase_service and legacy artifact behavior remains unchanged.
Acceptance package and Skill validators pass.
The terminal validator passes and does not authorize acceptance, release, or archive.

slices.recovery: Disable the toolchain policy and retain Phase behavior.
Remove the compact projector and preserve full-contract behavior.
Keep target implementation-complete and disable the new Acceptance entry.
